messages:
maria: quick field report — ran a fused/paged attention sweep on the h100 cluster and noticed a ~12% p99 regression when using the interleaved KV layout with bfloat16. repro harness attached below. :thinking:

ajay: ugh. is this on fused-flash or the paged-fusion path?

maria: paged-fusion path (the codepath that falls back to page fusion for long contexts). fused-flash unaffected. regression appears only when stride != 1 for KV (we're seeing odd L2/L1 miss patterns).

sasha: microbench numbers I ran this morning:
```
# microbench quick summary (A100/h100)
config: seq=1024, batch=8, kv_layout=interleaved, dtype=bfloat16
fused-flash:  token/s= 1140  p50=14ms  p99=28ms
paged-fusion: token/s=  980  p50=16ms  p99=31ms  <-- +12% p99 vs baseline
paged-fusion (separate-kv): token/s=1020  p50=15ms  p99=27ms
```
Looks like separate (segregated) KV improves the p99.

taylor: interesting. did you try padding alignment to 64/128 bytes? might be a coalescing/wrap issue on the paged allocator. also what allocator are you on (cudaMallocAsync vs pooled)?

maria: pooled allocator. I bisected to commit abc1234 -> the change was the interleaved write reordering for smaller batches. I suspect the stride layout + reordering interacts badly with the page coalescer.

ajay: can you paste a short perf report (nvprof / Nsight summary)? even a rough L2/DRAM breakdown will help.
\maria: pasted flame-lite output from perf-bot:
```
perf-bot: flame: paged-fusion interleaved bfloat16
L2_TEX_HIT_RATE: 0.78
L2_TEX_MISS: 15432
DRAM_READS: 2.1e7
warp_serialize: 0.03
mem_stall_long: 0.12
note: compare to separate-kv: L2_TEX_MISS: 11200  DRAM_READS:1.7e7
```

perf-bot: automated hint: try adding 128-byte padding to each KV row and re-run fused->paged conversion. Also try forcing stride to 1 in the interleave writer (temporary) to see if misses drop.

sasha: I did a quick experiment adding 128B pad: p99 dropped from 31ms -> 26ms, but token/s decreased slightly (1-2%) due to extra mem throughput.

taylor: tradeoff seems clear: alignment padding reduces cache churn but increases bandwidth. for production path we could: 1) keep interleaved for small-batch fast path, 2) switch to separate layout when page-fusion engaged OR when stride != 1 OR when dtype=bfloat16. That heuristic is easy to add to kernel selector.

ajay: agree. also consider a runtime flag to force_stride=1 for interleaved writer as a short-term mitigation. we should add a perf regression test that covers seq>=512 + interleaved + bfloat16 so CI catches this.

maria: will open a PR with: diagnostic flags, 128B pad experiment branch, and kernel-selector heuristic that prefers separate-kv for paged-fusion/bfloat16.

sasha: +1. I'll add the microbench harness to eng-runtime/benchmarks and a small CI check.

deply-bot: deploy check: no rollout until we validate on h100 staging.

taylor: also add a quick e2e eval for cost: paddings increase memory by ~3-5% for our common configs; include that in PR.

maria: plan: PR by EOD, staging runs tomorrow AM, canary if green. thanks all. :thumbsup:
